subject: biology-2
question: A **prion** is an infectious agent made entirely of misfolded protein. How does a prion propagate and create more prions inside an infected animal?

options.text: It is a naked RNA molecule that hijacks the cell's ribosomes to copy itself.
It carries DNA genes that direct the cell to build new misfolded proteins.
The misfolded prion contacts a normal protein of the same kind and refolds it into the abnormal shape, starting a chain reaction.
The prion mutates the host's genes so that every new protein the cell makes is misfolded.

explanation: A prion spreads by acting as a template that refolds normal copies of the same protein into the abnormal shape, so one prion becomes many. A describes a viroid, which is RNA. B is false because prions contain no nucleic acid. D is false because prions do not mutate host genes.
